original_question: Is every nontrivial Segal algebra non-approximately amenable?
target_in_paper: Question 12 in Section 4.1 (Algebras associated to locally compact groups): "Is it true that every nontrivial Segal algebra is not approximately amenable?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost verbatim: it asks for a universal negation of approximate amenability for nontrivial Segal algebras, which is exactly the content of Question 12.
missing_details: The paper is working in the setting of Banach algebras associated to locally compact groups; the relevant objects are Segal algebras S^1(G) on a locally compact group G.
"Nontrivial" is left implicit in the draft; here it means a proper Segal algebra, i.e. not the whole ambient group algebra L^1(G).
The quantifier is over all locally compact groups G and all Segal algebras S^1(G) on G.
The Banach-algebra structure under discussion is the usual convolution structure inherited from L^1(G).
The paper's formulation is specifically about approximate amenability, not pseudo-amenability or bounded approximate amenability.
No extra assumptions such as symmetry, abelianness, compactness, SIN, or amenability of G are part of Question 12.
refined_question: For every locally compact group G and every proper Segal algebra S^1(G) on G (equivalently, every nontrivial Segal subalgebra of L^1(G), with its usual convolution Banach-algebra structure), must S^1(G) fail to be approximately amenable?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper's Question 12. The nearby context in Section 4.1 first fixes the Segal-algebra setting by stating Theorem 4.3 for a Segal algebra S^1(G) on a locally compact group G, including the necessary condition that pseudo-amenability or approximate amenability of S^1(G) forces G to be amenable. Immediately afterward, after listing several partial non-approximate-amenability results, the paper asks exactly whether every nontrivial Segal algebra is not approximately amenable. The immediately preceding sentence also invokes Theorem 3.3(2) to explain that a nontrivial Segal algebra cannot even be boundedly approximately contractible because it has no bounded approximate identity. So the only sharpening needed is to make explicit the ambient locally compact group setting, the notation S^1(G), and the meaning of "nontrivial" as proper.
